open_points.subject: R0-12 binary-delivery failure classification
open_points.text: “a refused document read answers that way also when its stored content is missing, oversize or unlisted, while a photo whose stored content cannot be delivered fails as an explicit storage-unavailable error” does not define which failures count as a photo whose content “cannot be delivered,” or how document storage failures outside the three named cases are classified.
open_points.question: For each post-authorization failure—missing object, storage I/O failure, oversize content, and recognized-but-unlisted media type—must a document use the concealed response and must a photo use the explicit storage-unavailable error, or do some failures receive another rejection?
options: All post-authorization delivery failures are concealed for documents and explicit storage-unavailable for photos.
Only missing, oversize and unlisted document failures are concealed; other document storage failures are explicit, while every photo delivery failure is storage-unavailable.
Only missing or storage-access failures are storage-unavailable for photos; oversize and unlisted photo content use separate content-policy rejections.
open_points.default_guess: Conceal the three expressly named document failures, report other document storage I/O failures as storage-unavailable, and report every post-authorization photo storage, size or media-type failure as storage-unavailable.

witness.initial: An authorized viewer requests a client-visible ProgressPhoto whose stored bytes have a GIF signature, which is outside the permitted photo media-type list.
events: The viewer requests the photo by photo_id.
The owning photo module authorizes the viewer and passes the stored reference to binary storage.
Binary storage recognizes GIF and refuses delivery because GIF is unlisted.
outcomes: The request fails with the explicit storage-unavailable error because the photo's stored content cannot be delivered.
The request fails with a distinct unsupported-media/content-policy rejection because A14 separately calls unlisted content “rejected.”
witness.observer: The authenticated viewer sees a different public error classification or HTTP response.
